exercises.label: Discovery Playground — Ordinal number crossword puzzle
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Pair up and work with your partner to complete this ordinal number crossword puzzle.
items: Worked example (already filled in, struck through in clue list): 1-Down = 11th, 8-Across = 19th
exercises.answer_key: Worked examples (given): 1-Down = ELEVENTH, 8-Across = NINETEENTH. Remaining answers (computed): Across 6 (13th) = THIRTEENTH; Across 9 (12th) = TWELFTH; Across 10 (18th) = EIGHTEENTH; Down 2 (20th) = TWENTIETH; Down 3 (14th) = FOURTEENTH; Down 4 (17th) = SEVENTEENTH; Down 5 (16th) = SIXTEENTH; Down 7 (15th) = FIFTEENTH.

illustrations.description: Small circular icon of a character with a telescope, beside the 'Discovery Playground' heading.
illustrations.pedagogical_role: section icon for the paired crossword activity

illustrations.description: A crossword-puzzle grid with numbered clue cells (1-10, though not all numbers are used) arranged in an irregular interlocking pattern. Cell 1 (vertical, 8 letters) is pre-filled 'E L E V E N T H' with a hand-drawn orange arrow and the word 'Example' pointing at it. Cell 8 (horizontal, 10 letters, sharing its 3rd letter with cell 1's 8th letter 'H') is pre-filled 'N I N E T E E N T H'. All other numbered cells (2,3,4,5,6,7,9,10) are empty for students to fill in.
illustrations.pedagogical_role: the puzzle itself; two answers are pre-solved as worked examples
illustrations.text_in_image: ELEVENTH (1-down, filled); NINETEENTH (8-across, filled); numbers 1-10 as clue-cell labels; 'Example' hand-written callout

visual_layout_notes: Blue 'Discovery Playground' heading with telescope icon at top, instruction line below, then a large interlocking crossword grid roughly centred on the page, with 'Across' and 'Down' clue-number lists at the bottom (clue 1-Down and clue 8-Across are struck through as already-solved worked examples). Footer '22' centred at bottom.
flags: Exact cell-by-cell grid geometry (which columns each Down word occupies, where each Across word starts/ends) was not reverse-engineered pixel-by-pixel; each clue's answer word was computed directly from its printed ordinal-number clue (e.g. '13th'->THIRTEENTH), which is authoritative and unambiguous regardless of grid layout.
